cves.d: A vulnerability was identified in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. Affected by this vulnerability is the function plugins.install_package of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. Such manipulation leads to null pointer dereference. The attack may be performed from remote. Upgrading the affected component is advised. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A vulnerability was determined in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. Affected is the function plugins.get_package_info of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. This manipulation causes null pointer dereference. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A flaw was found in the Keycloak Operator. Deterministic hashes derived from Kubernetes Secrets are published in generated StatefulSet metadata and in KeycloakOIDCClient status. A user with read access to those resources may be able to recover a low-entropy credential referenced by a Secret, even when Kubernetes RBAC denies the user access to the Secret itself.
Enforce a recursion limit in Unmarshal to prevent stack exhaustion when parsing deeply-nested, recursive structures.
Decoding a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words can consume excessive CPU.

A vulnerability was found in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. This impacts the function ovpn-client.set_group of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. The manipulation results in null pointer dereference. The attack can be executed remotely. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A vulnerability has been found in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. This affects the function ovpn-client.get_third_config of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. The manipulation leads to null pointer dereference. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

WWW::Form::UrlEncoded::XS versions before 0.28 for Perl write past the end of the Perl argument stack when parse_urlencoded returns many pairs.

parse_urlencoded returns its result as a list, pushing each decoded key and value onto the argument stack without first extending the stack to fit them. parse_urlencoded_arrayref returns an array reference and is not affected.

A remote client that sends a query string or request body with many pairs to an application parsing it with parse_urlencoded can corrupt memory and crash the process.

Plane is an open-source project management tool. In versions prior to 1.4.0, the v2 asset static endpoint allows unauthenticated requests and returns presigned S3 URLs for an asset with access-signed parameters. Any user who knows an asset UUID can retrieve the signed URL without an account, providing access to that asset. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.0.

WWW::Form::UrlEncoded::XS versions before 0.27 for Perl read one byte before the input buffer when parsing an empty string.

parse_urlencoded and parse_urlencoded_arrayref check for a trailing "&" or ";" by reading the last byte of the input, without first checking that the input has any bytes.

A remote client that sends an empty query string or request body to an application parsing it with this module can crash the process.

A flaw was found in GStreamer gst-plugins-good (avidemux). In the subindex parser, missing validation of the entry count can cause excessive memory allocation and denial of service. Because avidemux is auto-plugged by playbin, decodebin, and gst-discoverer, opening or previewing a crafted AVI is sufficient to trigger the issue. Fixed upstream in gst-plugins-good 1.28.6 (GStreamer-SA-2026-0072).

A flaw was found in GStreamer gst-plugins-good (avidemux). In the superindex and subindex parsers, integer overflow can bypass bounds checks and cause out-of-bounds reads. Because avidemux is auto-plugged by playbin, decodebin, and gst-discoverer, opening or previewing a crafted AVI is sufficient to trigger the issue. Fixed upstream in gst-plugins-good 1.28.6 (GStreamer-SA-2026-0072).

A flaw was found in GStreamer gst-plugins-good (avidemux). In the Nikon metadata tag parser, a pointer can be dereferenced without verifying that data remains in the buffer, causing out-of-bounds reads. Because avidemux is auto-plugged by playbin, decodebin, and gst-discoverer, opening or previewing a crafted AVI is sufficient to trigger the issue. Fixed upstream in gst-plugins-good 1.28.6 (GStreamer-SA-2026-0072).

PDF::API2 versions before 2.049 for Perl allow unbounded recursion via circular cross-reference chains in readxrtr.

When a PDF is opened, readxrtr reads each cross-reference table and calls itself on the offset in the trailer's /Prev entry. Nothing records which offsets it has already read, so a /Prev entry pointing back to an earlier table, or to its own, makes it recurse without end.

An attacker who supplies a crafted PDF can cause a denial of service in any application that opens it.

A flaw has been found in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. The impacted element is the function ovpn-client.add_group of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. Executing a manipulation can lead to null pointer dereference. The attack may be launched remotely. The affected component should be upgraded. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.024 for Perl skip issuer, subject, audience and JWT ID checks when the claim is absent or the option is a plain string.

decode_jwt runs the verify_iss, verify_sub, verify_aud and verify_jti checks only when the token carries the claim, and honours an option only as a Regexp or CODE reference. Any other value, such as verify_aud => 'myapp', is ignored.

An application that relies on these checks accepts a validly signed token meant for a different issuer, subject or audience.

Missing integrity verification vulnerabilities exist in the command line interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) that could be exploited by a low-privileged local attacker if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to modify certain system data.

A weak cryptography vulnerability exists in HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated remote attacker with high privileges to obtain sensitive information from the affected system if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met.

A vulnerability in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to conduct a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attack against a user of the interface. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary script code in a victim's browser in the context of the web interface.

Missing authorization vulnerabilities exist in the API of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated attacker with low privileges to modify data on the affected system.

An XML external entity (XXE) vulnerability exists in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated remote attacker with low privileges to obtain sensitive information from the affected system.

Path traversal vulnerabilities exist in the web-based management interface and API of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave), which could be exploited by an authenticated attacker with low privileges. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to read certain files on the underlying operating system.

Improper certificate validation vulnerabilities in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to circumvent existing authentication controls if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to gain administrative access to the affected system.

A command injection vulnerability exists in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated remote attacker with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met.

A sensitive information disclosure vulnerability exists in the affected interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain sensitive information from the affected system.

A missing integrity verification vulnerability exists in HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow a low-privileged local attacker to modify trusted system data on the affected system.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded inflation of zip DEF payloads.

When a token header sets "zip" to "DEF", decode_jwt inflates the payload with no limit on the output size. A signed token is inflated after its signature verifies. An encrypted token is inflated after decryption, and with RSA-OAEP or ECDH-ES key management anyone who holds the recipient's public key can produce a token that decrypts.

Authenticated SQL injection vulnerabilities in the web-based management interface and API of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) could allow a low-privileged authenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary SQL statements against HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information from and modify data on the affected system.

A vulnerability in a system functionality could allow a low-privilege authenticated attacker with network access to potentially authenticate as an unintended user. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to gain unauthorized access, potentially affecting system integrity, exposing sensitive information, or disrupting management operations.

A command injection vulnerability exists in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system of the affected system, impacting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of HPE Networking Management Software (AirWave).

A vulnerability in system functionality could allow an attacker with network access to bypass authentication. Successful exploitation could potentially allow an attacker to perform unauthorized actions, affecting system integrity and confidentiality.

An authentication bypass vulnerability exists in the web management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to gain unauthorized administrative access to the affected system, impacting the confidentiality and integrity of AirWave.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via an unbounded PBES2 iteration count.

For a token using a PBES2 key management algorithm, decode_jwt passes the p2c header parameter to PBKDF2 as the iteration count without a range check, and derives the key before any integrity check. Unless accepted_alg rules it out, a token can select PBES2 whenever decode_jwt is given a symmetric key.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl compare HMAC signatures and JWE authentication tags in non-constant time.

decode_jwt compares HS256, HS384 and HS512 signatures, and the authentication tag of A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384 and A256CBC-HS512 encrypted tokens, against the computed value with Perl's eq operator. Its run time depends on the number of matching leading bytes.

An attacker who can submit many candidate tokens and measure the timing precisely enough may recover the expected signature or tag byte by byte and forge a token that verifies.

psqlODBC rewrites statement text for keyset-driven cursors and ODBC escapes using positions it found in the text. These positions could lie outside the text or describe another statement:

- After SQLExecDirect() failed on a statement handle, the FROM and WHERE positions of the failed statement were applied to the next, shorter statement on that handle.
- The parser could record a FROM position with no text after it, and the rewrite then copied a negative length.
- An {fn …} escape whose arguments contain FOR UPDATE, ; or INTO … FROM made the driver remove a cursor prefix from the wrong buffer.
- {fn CONVERT(?, …)} with an output parameter produced a negative argument length.
- An unclosed {fn …} escape made the driver read past the statement, and a few thousand nested ones exhausted the stack.
- Translating @@identity in long statement text read an uninitialised pointer, and {? = call …} with nothing bound for the return value dereferenced NULL.

Whoever supplies the text of a statement that an application opens on a keyset-driven or dynamic cursor with a concurrency other than read-only, or calls with an output parameter, can corrupt the application's heap and end it. That includes the users of query tools, report builders and other applications that run SQL their users type. Code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC assumed that a table it reads keeps the definition it had when the statement was described or parsed. A database user who owns a table or view another user's application reads can crash that application, with an honest server and default options, in these cases:

- Columns dropped or added in another session while the application updates rows through an updatable cursor, or describes the columns with Parse=1.
- A view whose ctid is NULL, read through an updatable cursor, which writes past the row cache, and a view with a volatile filter scrolled backward with UseDeclareFetch=1.
- Rows added through an updatable cursor to a table with child tables or partitions.
- A column whose type is named lo, written with data-at-execution parameters.
- A DROP TABLE or ALTER TABLE on the connection while another statement still uses the table's column information.
- NULL key columns in rows the driver re-reads for an updatable cursor.
- A function called with more output parameters than its result has columns.
- SQLTables() and SQLTablesW() dereferenced NULL when called with empty strings for the catalog, schema and table names together with a NULL TableType, which kills the process that loaded the driver and every session it serves.

The demonstrated results are crashes; one case writes past a heap buffer, but code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

When Debug or CommLog is enabled and the log directory cannot be used, psqlODBC falls back to a directory under the user's home directory. It wrote that path with an unexpanded ~, which is resolved relative to the process's current directory. Another local user who controls a directory on that path can make the driver create the victim's mylog_*.log and psqlodbc_*.log files in any directory the victim can write to, or leave the victim's process blocked in open().

This completes the fix for CVE-2026-120066 in 18.00.0006.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

With SQL_C_DEFAULT, the C type of a bound column or parameter follows its SQL type. An application sizes its buffer from the type it was told when it described the statement. When the column had another type at fetch time, because the server reported another type, the table was altered, or an output parameter's result column had another type, psqlODBC wrote the larger type into the smaller buffer: 12 bytes past a 4-byte buffer for a uuid, and more in multi-row fetches, where the driver also steps through the array by the larger size.

Other conversions wrote past the application's buffer as well:

- With Int8As set to a smaller type, an int8 column fetched as SQL_C_DEFAULT was still written as 8 bytes.
- An int2vector column fetched as SQL_C_DEFAULT returned unterminated binary data instead of text.
- An output parameter that the application discards by binding a NULL buffer overflowed a stack buffer in the driver.
- SQLGetData() with BufferLength 0 on a column the driver reads as a large object wrote a NUL byte past the buffer.
- Adding a row with SQLBulkOperations(SQL_ADD) on a static updatable cursor before the first fetch, then changing that row, rolling back and fetching it, made the keyset index arithmetic free a pointer that was never allocated and corrupt the heap.

This can be triggered by a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable), and by the owner of a table the application reads.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC mapped an SSLmode value in a connection string that it did not recognise, such as SSLmode=Require, SSLmode=Verify-Full, SSLmode={require} or SSLmode={verify-full}, to disable. SQLDriverConnect() then returned SQL_SUCCESS with no diagnostic, and the connection was not encrypted.

An attacker on the network path of such a connection can read and change its traffic.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

A parameter-array execution that fails part-way leaves the rows it has already
queued on the statement handle, and the next execution on that handle sends
them. After a data-at-execution batch is abandoned, by SQLCancel or a
rejected SQLPutData, the next SQLExecDirect sends the failed batch's rows
and returns SQL_SUCCESS without sending its own statement.

So an application that logs the failure on the same handle has its log entry
turned into a silent no-op, while rows it was told had failed are stored. An
end user who controls one value in an application's array insert can arrange
both halves of that.

A second route needs no data-at-execution parameter: when building a later row
fails in parameter conversion, the queued rows go to the server ahead of the
next parameter array on the handle, inside whatever transaction and session
settings are current by then. One variant also writes past the end of a shorter
SQL_ATTR_PARAM_STATUS_PTR array supplied by the next statement.

The statements that run are the application's own, correctly quoted; no SQL
text comes from outside.

Versions from psqlODBC 12.02.0000, which introduced batched parameter-array
execution, up to and including 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC did not check that a server reply matches the query it sent: that a FETCH returns no more rows than it asked for, that each row has the described number of columns, that one query produces one result, and that a COPY, a transaction or the connection ends where the protocol says. By sending replies that do not match, a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable) can corrupt memory in the application:

- A FETCH reply with more rows than requested overflows the row cache.
- Extra results in reply to a FETCH, or to the queries of a keyset-driven cursor, are freed while still in use.
- A key query of a keyset-driven cursor answered with extra columns, or a re-read row with fewer columns, overflows the row cache.
- Replies without columns or rows, or with NULL values, to the driver's internal queries at connect time and in catalog functions are dereferenced.
- A malformed relacl value in SQLTablePrivileges() makes the driver write past a buffer.
- On Windows with MSDTC, a long transaction name returned by the server overflows a buffer during recovery.
- Values in replies to the driver's internal queries are used without checking their range: an empty column name, a parameter count, a large-object size, a function's or trigger's argument count, and a result of exactly 32767 columns. They are dereferenced, read past, returned to the application or sent back to the server as stack memory, or make the driver loop forever.
- A reply that ends a COPY, the connection or the transaction at an unexpected point leaves freed results, keysets or table information in use: a CopyOutResponse followed by a lost connection, a ROLLBACK command tag under UseDeclareFetch=1, or a lost connection while a cursor with positioned updates is closed. Eight extra bytes in a reply also make the driver wait forever for a COPY to end.
- On Windows, a start-up reply without client_encoding crashes the driver, and with MSDTC a failed connection makes the XA library use a connection it has already freed.
- An error message ending in the first byte of a multibyte character leaves the SQLSTATE returned by SQLGetDiagRecW() unterminated.
- When a string value did not fit the application's buffer, eight Unicode entry points filled the buffer and wrote no null terminator, so a caller that reads to the terminator, as ODBC allows, read past the end of its own buffer.

This continues the fixes for CVE-2026-120058 and CVE-2026-120060, which covered other replies. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

On Windows, when a connection takes part in a distributed transaction, psqlODBC and its XA library open further connections of their own to finish the transaction. These connections did not keep the security settings of the application's connection:

- When the XA library's first connection attempt failed, it tried again with sslmode=allow, even for a data source configured with sslmode=verify-full or verify-ca.
- The connections the driver opens itself ignored every libpq option given through pqopt, such as channel_binding=require, and the open string it registers with MSDTC carried no pqopt, so the XA library's connections dropped those options too.

An attacker on the network path between the MSDTC host and the PostgreSQL server, without a certificate or credentials, can make those connections go to a server of their choosing without TLS, read and change what they send, and decide the outcome MSDTC records for the transaction.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC parsed and built connection strings in ways that let a value end early:

- In a braced value, such as PWD={…}, a trailing byte 0x7d of a GBK, Big5 or SJIS character was taken for the closing brace.
- A braced value that ended right after an escaped }} was not reported as unterminated, and its contents were parsed as further keywords.
- SQLConnectW(), SQLDriverConnectW() and SQLBrowseConnectW() cut a connection string whose UTF-8 form is longer than 32767 bytes, which changes how the rest of it is parsed.
- On Windows with MSDTC, the password and user name were put into the XA open string without escaping, and the XA library copied each item of that string into a 64-byte stack buffer.
- Percent-encoding a long password wrote one byte past a 4096-byte stack buffer.

An end user who supplies a password, or another value the application puts into the connection string, can set other connection keywords, for example to connect the application to a server of their choosing. The MSDTC case can also overflow a stack buffer in the process that loads the XA library.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC uses sizes and counts without checking their range, or keeps them in types too small for them:

- A row array size of 0, set with SQLSetStmtAttr() or on the ARD, makes SQLSetPos() with SQL_REFRESH write past the bound arrays.
- SQL_DESC_COUNT above 32767 on an APD or IPD writes before the start of a heap buffer.
- A numeric parameter with a negative scale overflows a stack buffer.
- SQLGetData() of a text value of 2 GiB or more into a wide-character buffer computes a wrapped size and overflows the heap.
- The 16-bit reference count and size of the statement parser's column-information cache wrap, which frees a cache entry still in use or overflows the cache, and a statement with more than 32768 columns overflows the parser's field array.
- An updatable cursor that records more than 65535 changes in one transaction wraps the 16-bit capacity of its rollback log, which overflows it and frees it twice.
- A statement with 32769 or more parameter markers overflows a 16-bit parameter count.
- A wide-character string of more than 2 GiB wraps the size of its UTF-8 conversion, which is then written below the start of a heap buffer.
- SQLGetDiagField() and SQLGetDiagFieldW() always stored the five-character SQLSTATE plus its terminator and checked BufferLength only afterwards, overrunning a buffer shorter than six bytes.
- The ANSI SQLSetDescField(SQL_DESC_NAME) on an IPD ignored BufferLength and copied the name with strdup(), reading a name passed as pointer plus length past its end.
- SQLFetchScroll(SQL_FETCH_BOOKMARK) did not check the bookmark it was given, so whoever chooses the bookmark value read out of bounds and crashed the process.
- Four places in the parameter conversion read one byte past the end of a bound character parameter, and one of them rewrote it.
- Binding a date, time or timestamp C value to an SQL_INTEGER or SQL_SMALLINT parameter dereferenced NULL instead of returning the conversion error.

Depending on the case, the values come from the application, from the data or statement text an end user supplies, or from a database user who controls the size of a table or value. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

With the driver's debug log (MyLog) turned on, two paths write the database
password to the log in clear text, both beside a line where the driver's own
redaction masks it as PWD=xxxxx:

- Pressing "Test" in the Windows data source setup dialog (psqlsetup.dll)
  logs the whole connection string, which carries PWD= percent-encoded,
  which is reversible, and any password= or sslpassword= inside pqopt.
- The Unicode connect functions SQLDriverConnectW, SQLConnectW and
  SQLBrowseConnectW log their arguments as they convert them between UTF-16
  and UTF-8, before the masking happens. The ANSI entry points are unaffected.

Turning the log on takes an administrator, and MyLog is off by default. The
exposure is the person who later reads the log, which in practice means a log
attached to a bug report or handed to support. Making that safe is the purpose
of the driver's redaction, and these two sites bypassed it.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC frees memory that is still in use, frees it twice, or writes outside an application buffer in these cases:

- The clean-up the driver runs at commit and rollback sends queries of its own, and the reply to one of them can start the clean-up again while it is running. The nested run frees the rollback log, or the list of cursors and prepared statements to close, and the outer run uses and frees it again.
- The callback through which libpq delivers notices could run that clean-up, and close the connection, while libpq was still using the connection.
- Freeing a statement whose result holds several cursors (FetchRefcursors=1, or UseDeclareFetch=1) used the freed first result while the later cursors were closed.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, after a rollback closed an updatable cursor, rows added or deleted through it were counted but not stored, so freeing the statement freed uninitialised pointers, and adding a row wrote past the keyset.
- After a multi-row fetch failed on a row other than the first of its rowset, SQLGetData() wrote at an offset past the buffer the application passed.
- SQLProcedureColumns() freed the result of its catalog query twice when the query failed.
- In a process named sqlservr (SQL Server linked servers), a server version below 8.4 made the statement parser free a buffer twice.
- A failed SQLPutData in the middle of a SQLSetPos() or SQLBulkOperations() data-at-execution sequence left the whole operation pending, with the internal statement still allocated and autocommit silently off, so later statements were rolled back at disconnect. The next positioned update ran the stale callback against a statement that was never executed and dereferenced NULL.

Most of these can be triggered by a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable). A database user who can make a statement fail, or who controls the contents of a row the application reads, can trigger the UseDeclareFetch=1 and SQLGetData() cases against an honest server. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC scans statement text itself to substitute parameters, translate ODBC escapes, join batched statements and rewrite queries for updatable cursors. Where it read the text differently from the server, text the driver took for data ran as SQL, or a positioned write went to another table:

- An escape string constant written e'…' in lower case was not recognised as one, and '…' after a keyword ending in E, as in LIKE'…', was taken for one.
- A } inside a quoted literal ended an ODBC {d …}, {t …}, {ts …} or {escape …} sequence.
- Dollar-quote tags containing _ were not recognised, and an identifier starting with _ followed by $, such as _$$, was taken for the start of a dollar quote, so a parameter marker inside a literal was substituted.
- A trailing -- comment in one statement of a batched parameter array swallowed the next statement.
- Comments, literals longer than 255 bytes and escape strings were misread when the driver located the FROM and WHERE clauses of a query for an updatable cursor, and the text copied into the cursor's own queries could include SQL from inside a literal.
- A table name containing $ was cut at the $, and a quoted table name starting with , or ; ended the table list, so positioned updates, inserts and deletes went to another table.
- An integer parameter with an embedded NUL byte cut the query short.
- /*/ was taken for a comment that opens and closes, while the server reads it as one that only opens.
- ConnSettings was split at every semicolon, including one inside a quoted literal, so an application that puts an end user's value into a SET command there ran the rest of the value as SQL at connect time.

An end user who controls text the application puts into a statement, or a parameter value, can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. A database user who can create a table with a crafted name can redirect another user's positioned writes to a table of their choosing.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

To build positioned updates and to describe columns, psqlODBC matches the names in a statement against the catalog. Where it matched differently from the server, it used another table or column:

- Table and schema names were compared case-insensitively in its column-information cache, so users could be taken for another user's "Users", and the driver then evaluated that table's column default to answer @@IDENTITY.
- In FROM ONLY t, ONLY was taken for the table name.
- Column names were compared case-insensitively, so with Parse=1 the type of another column could decide the size of the application's buffer, which a fetch then overflowed.
- In a database whose encoding is single-byte, such as LATIN1 or SQL_ASCII, the server folds the accented letters of an unquoted name by its own locale, while the driver folded only A-Z, so ÉTAT could be taken for another user's "État" instead of état.
- On systems other than Windows, in a Turkish or Azeri locale, an unquoted I was not folded to i, and keywords and ODBC function names did not match.
- Without a schema name, SQLSpecialColumns() could report the key columns of another user's same-named temporary table, and SQLPrimaryKeys() could take another user's index named <table>_pkey for the primary key of a table without one.
- After search_path changed other than through a plain SET statement, positioned writes went to the same-named table in the previously current schema.
- SQLBulkOperations() trusted the ctid stored inside a variable-length bookmark handed back by the application, and ignored the WHERE clause that restricted the cursor, so a forged bookmark read, updated or deleted any row of the cursor's table.

A database user who can create a table in a schema on another user's search_path can redirect that user's positioned updates, inserts and deletes to a table of their choosing, where they run with the victim's rights, or run an expression of their choosing under the victim's role.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

To escape a bound parameter, or a name passed to a catalog function, psqlODBC has to know where each multibyte character of the client encoding ends. It treated a client encoding named by an alias the server accepts, such as WIN950, Windows950 or big-5 for BIG5, as single-byte, and it accepted too narrow a range of lead bytes for JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR. A quote byte that the server reads as part of such a character was then not doubled, or a quote the server reads on its own was taken for part of a character, and the literal ended early.

An end user who controls one bound character parameter, or a name the application passes to a catalog function such as SQLTables(), can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. This requires a connection that is not in UTF-8: the ANSI driver, or the ANSI entry points, with one of these client encodings. For bound parameters the driver must also be substituting parameters itself, as it does with UseServerSidePrepare=0 or a cursor type other than forward-only.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC read memory it had not written, or memory past the end of an application buffer, and sent it to the server or returned it to the application:

- Text bound as SQL_C_CHAR to a large-object parameter was read past the end of the application's buffer, and the extra bytes were stored in the large object.
- After a fetch truncated a long bytea or large-object value, positioned updates and inserts read past the bound buffer and wrote that memory into the row.
- Hex text with a NUL byte, bound to a binary parameter with an explicit length, sent uninitialised heap memory as the parameter value.
- With RowVersioning=1, SQLColumns() on a table that does not exist returned uninitialised stack memory as the schema and table names.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, bookmarks of updatable block cursors contained uninitialised heap memory, and a malformed ctid from the server sent stale heap bytes in positioned updates and deletes.
- With UseServerSidePrepare=0, calling SQLNumResultCols(), SQLDescribeCol() or SQLColAttribute() on a prepared statement before SQLExecute() read the application's bound parameter buffers and sent their current contents to the server as literals, although ODBC lets the application fill those buffers after the describe.
- The driver named the prepared statements, savepoints, cursors and keyset plans it creates on the server after the heap addresses of its own objects, so the server, or anyone reading an unencrypted connection, learned exact heap addresses inside the client.

Depending on the case, an end user who supplies a parameter value, a database user who stores a long value in a row, or a hostile server can obtain memory of the application process, which may hold data of other users or credentials.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

A vulnerability was detected in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. The affected element is the function libcmcollect.set_traffic_config of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. Performing a manipulation results in null pointer dereference. The attack may be initiated remotely. You should upgrade the affected component. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

Incorrect authorization in affected versions of network-manager in Ubuntu allows a local attacker with code execution as the whoopsie user to invoke root-restricted D-Bus methods via an Ubuntu-specific D-Bus policy, disrupting network connectivity or altering network configuration.

  An Ubuntu-specific D-Bus policy configuration in NetworkManager granted the whoopsie user unrestricted send access to org.freedesktop.NetworkManager, overriding the default deny-list for root-only methods (SetLogging, Sleep, LoadConnections, and ReloadConnections). A local attacker able to execute code as the whoopsie user could exploit this to disrupt system networking or alter NetworkManager logging and connection configurations.

Comviva Revenue Plus (MobiLytix Customer Value Management) 3.0.0 contains an expression language injection vulnerability in the user administration module, where the POST /rp/manageUser endpoint handled by manageUsersAction evaluates the name of an arbitrary request parameter as a server-side Java EL expression before rendering the response. The only protection is a denylist of reflective method names, which does not cover constructor-based access to a JDK scripting engine, so authenticated low-privilege attackers can supply an EL expression as a parameter name to execute arbitrary operating system commands as the application server account. This product is no longer supported by the vendor; standard support ended on 2022-10-31 and extended support ended on 2023-10-31.

OpenRemote core before 1.34.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in UserAssetProvisioningMQTTHandler that allows unauthenticated attackers to impersonate provisioned devices without proof of private key possession. Attackers can publish a known device's public certificate to the provisioning request topic, authenticating their anonymous MQTT connection as the device's service account to read and modify assets.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in its filesystem storage bucket that only canonicalizes the bucket root, not descendant symlinks. Attackers can reference paths through a pre-existing symlink inside the bucket that pass the lexical prefix check, reading and writing files across the host filesystem.

Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Soroseo Soro & SEO Autopilot & AI Content Writer soro-seo allows Cross Site Request Forgery.This issue affects Soro & SEO Autopilot & AI Content Writer: from n/a through 1.4.3.
vp: soro & seo autopilot & ai content writer

cves.d: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass that allows users with the read-only VIEWER role to modify database schema, because CREATE on a nonexistent table implicitly defines it without the DEFINE TABLE permission check applied to explicit definitions. Authenticated VIEWER users can issue CREATE statements in non-STRICT databases to add arbitrary empty SCHEMALESS tables, cluttering schemas or colliding with application table names.

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows any user able to run queries to crash the server by triggering unchecked decimal overflow in math::sum or math::product. Attackers can submit a query summing or multiplying large decimal literals or aggregate stored decimals with GROUP ALL, causing a rust_decimal panic that terminates the entire server process.

SurrealDB from 3.2.0 before 3.3.4 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows record users to update protected rows by exploiting table-level PERMISSIONS FOR update predicates referencing COMPUTED fields. Because check_update_permissions evaluates the predicate before computed fields are populated, the field reads as NONE and deny-intended predicates like blocked != true pass, letting attackers modify records.

better-auth 1.3.7 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition in the emailOTP plugin attempt counter, collision-prone email change code keys, and accent-insensitive email lookups. Unauthenticated attackers can send concurrent guesses exceeding allowedAttempts to brute-force OTPs and sign in or reset passwords, signed-in users can verify addresses they do not own, and attackers receiving mail at accent-variant addresses can reset victims' passwords.

@better-auth/passkey 1.4.0-beta.16 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, and the passkey plugin in better-auth 1.2.0-beta.18 before 1.4.0, do not confirm WebAuthn user verification when userVerification is "required" and take the expected origin from the request instead of configuration. Users can register or use passkeys without the required PIN or biometric check, and passkey responses created on another origin under the same relying party ID may be accepted.

A flaw was found in ironic-image. The scripts responsible for constructing kernel parameters for CoreOS root file system (rootfs) and Ignition configuration URLs use a hardcoded `http://` scheme. This bypasses the intended Transport Layer Security (TLS) protection, even when TLS is enabled for the iPXE boot chain. An attacker on the local network segment can exploit this vulnerability by performing Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) spoofing to serve a malicious rootfs or intercept sensitive data, including SSH keys and secrets, from the Ignition configuration. This leads to a compromise of data integrity and confidentiality during the node provisioning process.

A flaw was found in maestro. A remote attacker could exploit a misconfiguration in the gRPC server where authentication defaults to a 'mock' mode. This default setting bypasses all authentication and authorization, allowing an unauthorized attacker to write resource bundles. Consequently, this could lead to arbitrary code execution on managed clusters.

ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the Redis protocol handler, which neither replies to nor closes a pre-authentication connection when it receives an array whose first element is not a string. Unauthenticated attackers can resend such an array just within the 30-second socket idle timeout to hold connections open indefinitely and exhaust RedisNetworkExecutor threads.

ArcadeDB native-image server builds 26.8.1 before 26.11.1 contain an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated clients to perform writes through read-only query paths by nesting statements in SELECT. Missing reflection metadata leaves SqlAstInspector with an empty AST, letting INSERT in projections or LET clauses persist via the query endpoint, MCP read-only mode, and HA follower routing.

A flaw was found in OpenSCAP. A heap-based buffer overflow can occur when processing a specially crafted Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) document using the sds-compose option. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to corrupt memory, resulting in an application crash and a Denial of Service (DoS).

actix-http 3.18.10 before 3.20.2 contains an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in its chunked decoder, which treats a bare LF after the last chunk as the start of a trailer section. Attackers can send a body ending in 0\r\n\n through a connection-reusing proxy so the next request's body is parsed as new requests, bypassing WAF or upstream protections.

A memory leak flaw was found in cockpit-ws. The login page handler leaks a heap allocation on every unauthenticated request that carries a CockpitLang cookie, allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to exhaust memory on the host and cause a denial of service.

cves.d: Rclone 1.49.0 before 1.76.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability in Proxy.Call that lets revoked users keep access because cached auth-proxy answers are never revalidated. Revoked users of serve sftp, ftp, http, or webdav can reconnect within five minutes using their original credentials to retain access indefinitely.

NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.08.0, the row-scoped endpoints of a public shared view check whether a target record exists by primary key without applying the view's row filter, while the view's list and count endpoints do apply it. A recipient of a shared-view link, including its password where one is configured, can list the linked records of a filtered-out record and obtain signed download paths for its attachments by guessing its primary key. This issue is fixed in version 2026.08.0.

XBackBone through 3.8.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to change other users' upload share codes via the POST /upload/{id}/vanity route. Attackers can supply sequential upload ids to MediaController::createVanity() to break existing share links and hijack the freed codes with their own uploads.

AzuraCast before 0.24.1 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the /api/station/{station_id}/profile/edit endpoint that exposes and accepts Icecast/Shoutcast passwords for users holding Manage Station Profile without Manage Station Broadcasting. Authenticated station users can read the admin, source, relay and streamer passwords via GET to administer Icecast or broadcast to listeners, or overwrite them via PUT to lock out operators.

Coder 2.6.0 before 2.29.26, 2.30.0 before 2.34.18, 2.35.0 before 2.37.10, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.6 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability because CSRF exemption patterns in coderd/httpmw/csrf.go are matched as unanchored regular expressions, letting affected API routes skip CSRF token and same-origin checks. Attackers controlling a page same-site with the deployment can make signed-in users' browsers send forged POST requests that recreate dev containers or add users whose names contain derp to organizations.

pypdf 2.4.2 before 7.0.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its handling of XFA forms that allows attackers to cause excessive memory consumption. Attackers can supply a crafted PDF containing XFA forms with many small fields so that loading the forms consumes large amounts of memory, causing a denial of service.

A vulnerability was determined in WPExperts New User Approve Plugin up to 3.3 on WordPress. Impacted is the function update_user_role of the file includes/end-points/class-users-api.php of the component REST API. Executing a manipulation can lead to missing authorization. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Faveo Helpdesk (Community) through 2.0.3 and 2.0.4.RC.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in ApiExceptAuthController::checkUrl(), reachable through the unauthenticated and unthrottled GET /api/v1/helpdesk/url route, which validates the url parameter only as a well-formed URL, appends the fixed path api/v1/helpdesk/check-url and fetches it with curl with TLS certificate verification disabled and no restriction on the target host, port or address range. Unauthenticated attackers can choose the scheme, host and port of the request to make the server connect to internal hosts and services, including loopback and private addresses, and read the response body, which is returned in the JSON result field.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Satellite (Foreman component). This vulnerability allows an authenticated user with edit_settings permissions to achieve arbitrary command execution on the underlying operating system via insufficient server-side validation of command whitelisting.

Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Assets module endpoints that return a depreciation schedule for a caller-supplied asset without checking read permission on that asset. Authenticated users can name another company's asset to disclose its purchase value, value after depreciation, and depreciation entries.
A flaw has been discovered in GnuTLS where an application crash can be induced when attempting to verify a specially crafted .pem bundle using the "certtool --verify-chain" command.
vp: red hat enterprise linux 9.2 extended update support

cves.d: A flaw was found in GnuTLS. The Minerva attack is a cryptographic vulnerability that exploits deterministic behavior in systems like GnuTLS, leading to side-channel leaks. In specific scenarios, such as when using the GNUTLS_PRIVKEY_FLAG_REPRODUCIBLE flag, it can result in a noticeable step in nonce size from 513 to 512 bits, exposing a potential timing side-channel.
vp: red hat enterprise linux 8.6 extended update support
red hat enterprise linux 8.8 extended update support
red hat enterprise linux 9.2 extended update support

cves.d: A flaw was found in the RPC library APIs of libvirt. The RPC server deserialization code allocates memory for arrays before the non-negative length check is performed by the C API entry points. Passing a negative length to the g_new0 function results in a crash due to the negative length being treated as a huge positive number. This flaw allows a local, unprivileged user to perform a denial of service attack by causing the libvirt daemon to crash.
vp: red hat enterprise linux 8 advanced virtualization

cves.d: An off-by-one error flaw was found in the udevListInterfacesByStatus() function in libvirt when the number of interfaces exceeds the size of the `names` array. This issue can be reproduced by sending specially crafted data to the libvirt daemon, allowing an unprivileged client to perform a denial of service attack by causing the libvirt daemon to crash.
vp: red hat enterprise linux 8 advanced virtualization

cves.d: A vulnerability was found in systemd-resolved. This issue may allow systemd-resolved to accept records of DNSSEC-signed domains even when they have no signature, allowing man-in-the-middles (or the upstream DNS resolver) to manipulate records.

Frappe ERPNext 12.7.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 stores imported Italian supplier e-invoices as public files in the Regional module, which the server returns without authentication. Unauthenticated attackers can request predictable file URLs built from the supplier's VAT number and invoice sequence to read supplier names, VAT numbers, bank account details and line items.

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.124.2 and 16.x before 16.53.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns item cost data without checking the caller's permissions on the item, company, or warehouse. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users restricted to other warehouses, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope items, companies, or warehouses to obtain valuation rates and average purchase costs.

Frappe ERPNext 14.0.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the CRM module because notes on Leads and Opportunities are saved without passing through the HTML sanitiser. Authenticated users with the Sales User role can save a note containing a crafted payload that executes in another user's session when they open the record, acting with that user's permissions.

Frappe ERPNext 10.1.41 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Manufacturing module endpoint that replaces BOMs without checking whether the caller may modify either BOM or the affected assemblies. Authenticated users who can create a BOM Update Log can send a crafted request naming two BOMs to replace the first with the second in every assembly site-wide.

Frappe ERPNext 15.10.4 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that checks whether an inventory number exists and creates missing Serial No and Batch master records without verifying create permission. Authenticated users can send a crafted request with a new number to create these records outside their role, affecting inventory data integrity.

Frappe ERPNext 6.3.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the customer and supplier portal list endpoint, which returns complete selling documents and RFQs without checking permission on the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can request out-of-scope records to read valuation, margin, and other bidder details.

diaspora* through 0.10.1, using the diaspora_federation gem through 1.2.0, contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to make the pod send requests to arbitrary internal hosts by supplying a crafted diaspora handle to the GET /link endpoint, which triggers WebFinger discovery without private-address filtering. Attackers can specify a handle containing an IPv4/IPv6 address and port such as diaspora://probe@host:port to force the HttpClient to connect to loopback, RFC1918, link-local, or cloud metadata addresses, enabling blind probing of the pod's internal network.

Frappe ERPNext 16.0.1 before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock dashboard chart endpoint that returns site-wide stock value when the caller has no permitted warehouse. Authenticated users with common operational roles can send crafted requests naming records outside their scope to read stock value data beyond their permissions.

Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.121.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read POS Profile cashier lists by calling a POS endpoint lacking record permission checks. Attackers, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope POS Profiles to retrieve their cashier data.

Handesk through 1.5 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the POST /webhook/bitbucket route, which is excluded from CSRF verification and processed by WebhookController::store() without validating any secret, signature, or request source before writing to the database. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted Bitbucket issue payloads referencing a linked roadmap Idea or ticket to alter the Idea's status or inject attacker-controlled notes attributed to the first administrator account.

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns uploaded bank statement file content without checking record-level permissions. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming records outside their scope to read full statement file contents.

Handesk through 1.5 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in Attachment::storeAttachmentFromRequest() that allows authenticated agents to upload files with arbitrary extensions by attaching them to ticket comments without extension, MIME type, or size validation. Attackers can upload a PHP file via POST /tickets/{ticket}/comments, which is stored under storage/app/public/attachments and served from /storage/attachments/, to achieve remote code execution as the web server user or serve malicious HTML/SVG content from the application origin.

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a POS endpoint that returns POS Opening Entries without verifying record-level read permissions. Authenticated users, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming other records to read open POS sessions of other users.

In gdm3 before 51.2, an improper privilege management vulnerability allows an unprivileged local attacker with an active GDM graphical session to execute arbitrary code as root by supplying a malicious environment variable during session reauthentication.

A vulnerability was found in D-Link R32 1.10B02. This affects an unknown function of the file /usr/bin/httpd of the component flupl self Endpoint. Performing a manipulation of the argument fpath results in os command injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

Frappe ERPNext 15.x 11.0.0-beta before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns Sales Order and Purchase Order values and counterparties without checking permissions on the requested records. Authenticated users, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read their order values and counterparties.

Frappe ERPNext 7.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in endpoints that build part of a query from caller-supplied sort parameters without validation. Authenticated low-privilege users can send crafted requests whose sort parameter holds SQL that the database executes as part of the query, extracting sensitive information.

A vulnerability in the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Shell implementation of Cisco UCS Servers and UCS-based appliances could allow an authenticated attacker with valid credentials for a user account with the role of user or admin or an unauthenticated attacker with physical access to an affected device to bypass UEFI Secure Boot validation checks and execute unauthorized software.

This vulnerability is due to the availability of memory write commands in the UEFI Shell while UEFI Secure Boot is enabled on a device. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by selecting the UEFI Shell boot option at boot time and using available shell commands to modify UEFI memory variables. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to manipulate the preboot environment, overwrite UEFI Secure Boot-related memory values, and execute unauthorized software on the affected device.
vp: cisco unified computing system e-series software (ucse)

cves.d: Frappe ERPNext before 15.124.2 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that records bank clearance dates, which checks only a broad role permission before writing to caller-named payment documents. Authenticated Accounts Users can send crafted requests naming payment documents of other companies, outside their User Permissions, or already submitted, to alter clearance dates and compromise bank reconciliation integrity.

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows non-admin users with settings:edit permission to modify OIDC provider configuration due to an improper permission check. Attackers can send a PUT request to /api/auth/oidc/<provider-id> setting adminClaim to their own OIDC group, gaining full admin access on their next OIDC login.

Hysteria 1.0.0 before 2.9.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in FragUDPMessage where UDP fragmentation fails to handle headers larger than the maximum datagram payload size. Authenticated clients can advertise a small max_datagram_frame_size and trigger a UDP response, causing a slice bounds panic that crashes the server.

web-token jwt-framework 1.2.0 before 3.4.10, jwt-experimental before 3.4.10, 4.0.x before 4.0.7, and 4.1.x before 4.1.7 contain a missing integrity check in the experimental Chacha20Poly1305 key-encryption algorithm, which discards the Poly1305 tag in encryptKey() and calls openssl_decrypt() without it in decryptKey(). Attackers on the token path can modify the encrypted content encryption key undetected.

A vulnerability was detected in eigent-ai eigent up to 1.0.2. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file backend/app/controller/chat_controller.py of the component Local Agent Control API. Performing a manipulation results in missing authentication. The attack may be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 1.0.3 addresses this issue. The patch is named 59f43afcb1b0ba7b2de8c65d585124f196c4aa17. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

In authd before 0.7.2, an improper access control vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to complete a first-time SSH login with another account's UID and incorrect primary GID, and to read or modify files owned by that account. This allows an attacker to access another account's data, potentially enabling account takeover or privilege escalation.

metasfresh through 5.175 contains a SQL injection vulnerability in the stressTest_massCacheInvalidation handler of DebugRestController, which concatenates the caller-supplied tableName request parameter into SELECT statements without parameterization or validation and only checks that the caller is authenticated. Authenticated WebUI users with any role can send GET requests to /rest/api/debug/stressTest/massCacheInvalidation with SQL in the tableName parameter to run time-based and error-based blind queries against the PostgreSQL database, extracting sensitive ERP data such as user credentials and financial records while also degrading availability through sleep payloads.

ChargePoint Home Flex Debug Interface With Improper Access Control Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows physically present attackers to bypass authentication on affected ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the serial debug interface. The issue results from the lack of access control prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to bypass authentication on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-28997.

ChargePoint Home Flex busybox Unnecessary Privileges Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the busybox binary. The issue results from the setuid flag being set. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29090.

ChargePoint Home Flex wpa_passphrase Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the PSK parameter passed to the wpa_passphrase endpoint. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29000.

ChargePoint Home Flex ssh Hard-coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the ssh service, which listens on TCP port 22 by default. The issue results from the use of hard-coded credentials. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to bypass authentication on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-28996.

ChargePoint Home Flex uploadsm filetype Link Following Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of the filetype parameter passed to the uploadsm endpoint. By creating a symbolic link, an attacker can abuse the service to write an arbitrary file. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29096.

ChargePoint Home Flex dwnldlogsm tar Command Injection Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the tar function. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29057.

A vulnerability has been found in D-Link R32 1.10B02. The impacted element is the function SetDeviceSettings of the file /usr/bin/httpd of the component DHMAPI Action Handler. RustDesk Client for Windows reg_recovery Missing Authorization Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of RustDesk Client for Windows. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the main IPC endpoint exposed by the RustDesk service. The issue results from the lack of authorization prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-34805.

The ITE it51xxx I2C driver, when operating as an I2C target (slave) in buffer mode (CONFIG_I2C_TARGET + CONFIG_I2C_TARGET_BUFFER_MODE), transmits response data from the fixed-size data->target_out_buffer inside its target FIFO interrupt handler target_i2c_isr_fifo() in drivers/i2c/i2c_ite_it51xxx.c. On every data interrupt of a host read transaction the handler pushes a fixed 16 bytes from target_out_buffer[i + data->r_index] into the hardware FIFO and then advances data->r_index by 16, without ever checking that index against the size of the buffer.

data->r_index is reset to zero only on a STOP or timeout condition, so within a single transaction it only accumulates. An I2C host that keeps clocking read bytes without issuing STOP drives data->r_index past the end of the buffer after sixteen interrupts (default CONFIG_I2C_TARGET_IT51XXX_MAX_BUF_SIZE = 256 bytes), and every interrupt after that reads 16 bytes from beyond target_out_buffer and places them on the bus. What follows the buffer in the driver's device data structure is data->target_shared_fifo and the remaining static device state, so a sufficiently long read transaction streams adjacent firmware memory to the host.

The same handler, and the shared-FIFO arm of target_i2c_isr_pio(), also declare the transfer length uninitialised and invoke the optional buf_read_requested() callback without checking that it is registered. A target that supplies no read callback leaves the source pointer NULL and the length indeterminate; when that length compares below the destination size, memcpy() runs with a NULL source. Because the transmit path feeds the FIFO whether or not the callback provided data, such a target also places whatever the previous request left in the buffer onto the bus.

The trigger is a malicious or misbehaving I2C master on the same bus (for example a compromised application processor or a rogue device on an exposed I2C bus); no software privilege on the victim is required and the handler runs in the target's kernel/firmware context. The disclosed bytes are not attacker-chosen, but their extent is: the host controls how long the transaction runs and therefore how far past the buffer the driver reads.

This is the read-direction counterpart of CVE-2026-14986, which closed the write direction of the same routine without adding the matching bound on the read path.

The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) receives sensor responses in the UART interrupt handler uart_cb_handler(). Once the 9-byte header has arrived, the handler reads the 16-bit package length from the header and uses it as the byte count for further uart_fifo_read() calls into rx_buf.data. It never checks that length against the destination buffer. That buffer is a union r502a_packet on the calling thread's stack, set up by transceive_packet(), and is only CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE + 12 bytes long (140 bytes by default).

A malicious or counterfeit sensor module, or an attacker who tampers with the UART wiring, can reply to any driver command with a header that declares a length of up to 65535 bytes. The ISR then writes that many attacker-supplied bytes past the end of the stack buffer. The existing length check in r502a_validate_rx_packet() runs only after the data has been written, so it does not prevent the overflow. Every sensor transaction is affected, including the ones issued by fps_init() during device initialization.

The result is a stack overwrite with attacker-controlled length and content in the calling thread. This can corrupt control data and may lead to arbitrary code execution on the host MCU, which would undermine any function the fingerprint sensor is meant to protect. The fix validates the declared length against CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE as soon as the header is complete and aborts the reception if it is out of range.

The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) points drv_data->rx_buf.data at an rx_packet buffer on the caller's stack and enables the UART RX interrupt before waiting 1500 ms for a reply. When the wait timed out, transceive_packet() returned -ETIMEDOUT but left the RX interrupt enabled and rx_buf.data still pointing at the caller's buffer.

Once the caller's frame has returned, any bytes that arrive late on the UART are written by the interrupt handler uart_cb_handler() through the dangling pointer into stack memory that the thread has since reused. The bytes come from the device on the other end of the UART. An attacker with physical access who replaces or impersonates the fingerprint module can trigger this by delaying a reply past the timeout and then sending a packet. A slow or faulty genuine module can also trigger it by accident.

The result is a write of attacker-chosen bytes into a live thread stack. The write length comes from the header of the late packet. Commit 96968fac22b, which landed together with this fix, bounds it to a header plus CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE bytes; affected releases do not have that bound. This can crash the device and may allow control-flow hijacking, depending on what occupies the reused stack region. The fix disables the RX interrupt, resets the RX semaphore and clears rx_buf.data on timeout, and the interrupt handler now refuses to write when no receive buffer is armed.

z_impl_pwm_capture_cycles() in drivers/pwm/pwm_capture.c stores its capture context (struct z_pwm_capture_cb_data, including a struct k_sem) on its own stack and registers a pointer to it as the driver capture callback's user_data. When called with a K_NO_WAIT timeout, k_sem_take() returns -EBUSY, which the function did not handle: it fell through, returned the uninitialized status field, copied uninitialized period/pulse values to the caller when that status happened to be zero, and returned without disabling the capture or clearing the callback.

pwm_capture_cycles() is a system call, and z_vrfy_pwm_capture_cycles() passes the caller's timeout through unchanged. With CONFIG_USERSPACE and CONFIG_PWM_CAPTURE enabled, an unprivileged user-mode thread that has been granted access to a capture-capable PWM device can pass K_NO_WAIT to trigger the defect. Without userspace the function is only reachable from trusted application code.

The uninitialized values come from the thread's privileged (kernel) stack, so a user-mode caller can read up to 8 bytes of stale kernel stack memory per call. More seriously, when the capture later completes, the driver ISR invokes z_pwm_capture_cycles_callback() with the dangling pointer. The callback writes into the expired kernel stack region and calls k_sem_give() on whatever memory now occupies it, which can corrupt live kernel stack frames and make the scheduler walk a forged wait queue. The result is kernel memory corruption from interrupt context, leading at least to a crash and possibly to privilege escalation out of the userspace sandbox. The fix rejects K_NO_WAIT with -EINVAL before any capture is configured.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.46 through 0.11.1, AutoPilot does not remove the media files that its block runs write to the executor's disk, leading to exhaustion. A signed-in user who can use AutoPilot can grow the temporary storage used by AutoPilot's tool process by about 1 GiB per chat. Once that filesystem is full, file handling fails for every user served by that executor and for anything else writing to the same disk. No other user's data is read or changed. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.2.

XO (Xen Orchestra) is a solution to visualize, manage, backup and delegate your XCP-ng (or XenServer) infrastructure. Prior to 6.9.2 and 6.10.1, REST cookie parsing turns authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D into {}. REST authentication passes that object to the XO token provider without requiring a string. The token collection treats {} as an unfiltered lookup and returns its first token; the provider authenticates as that token's owner if it is unexpired. The authenticated /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens route then returns reusable login token IDs. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.9.2 and 6.10.1.
